extra.message: The pageId parameter taken from the URL route /dashboard/<pageId> (controllers/Dashboard.py:8) is concatenated directly into the SQL query string ('SELECT pageId, title, content FROM pages WHERE pageId='+pageId) and executed via db.execute(). String concatenation allows arbitrary SQL injection.

request.url (attacker-controlled path) is interpolated into a Jinja2 template string via .format(request.url) on line 94, and the result is rendered with render_template_string() on line 95. An attacker can request a path containing Jinja2 directives (e.g. /{{7*7}}) to achieve server-side template injection leading to remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code (Code Injection)

extra.message: The system_call() function is registered globally as a Jinja2 context processor and invokes os.popen(command).read() with an arbitrary command argument. Because it is exposed to every template, any server-side template injection (e.g. the 404 SSTI) lets an attacker call system_call('{{...}}') to execute arbitrary OS commands. Exposing os.popen to the template context is a command injection risk.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command (OS Command Injection)

extra.message: User-supplied hex data from request.form['data_obj'] is decoded with bytes.fromhex(), written to ../pickle.hacker, and then deserialized with pickle.load() (line 27). pickle.load executes arbitrary code during unpickling, so an attacker can supply a malicious pickle payload to achieve remote code execution.

The <input> URL parameter is base64-decoded and passed to yaml.load() (line 18) without a SafeLoader. With PyYAML 3.13, yaml.load can instantiate arbitrary Python objects (e.g. !!python/object/apply), allowing remote code execution via the /information/<input> route.

User-controlled XML from request.form['customers'] is parsed with xml.dom.pulldom.parseString() without disabling external entity resolution. This allows an attacker to supply XML with external/entity definitions to read local files, perform SSRF, or cause denial of service (billion laughs).

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: The fileName value is taken directly from request.form['example_file'] and used in open(fileName, 'r') and send_file(fileName, ...) without any path validation. An attacker can supply an absolute path or traversal sequence (e.g. /etc/passwd or ../../etc/passwd) to read arbitrary files from the server.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory (Path Traversal)

extra.message: The uploaded file's filename (file.filename) is concatenated directly into the save path ('uploads/'+filename) on line 48. allowed_file() only validates the extension, not path separators, so an attacker can upload a file named e.g. ../../malicious.txt to write files outside the uploads directory (arbitrary file write).

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory (Path Traversal)

extra.message: The 'search' value originating from request.form.get('search') (controllers/Search.py:9) is rendered with {% autoescape false %}{{search}}{% endautoescape %}, disabling HTML escaping. The controller additionally sets the X-XSS-Protection header to '0' (Search.py:11). This allows reflected cross-site scripting.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (Cross-site Scripting)

extra.message: The user-submitted 'link' field (controllers/Messaging.py:16, stored via storeMessages) is rendered inside an href attribute: <a target="_blank" href="{{item[3]}}">. Jinja2 autoescaping does not neutralize javascript: URIs, so an attacker can store a value like javascript:alert(document.cookie) to achieve stored XSS when another user clicks the link.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (Cross-site Scripting)

extra.message: Content rendered on the about page uses {% autoescape false %} {{content}} {% endautoescape %}. The 'content' comes from pickle.load() of attacker-supplied data (controllers/About.py:27). If the deserialized object is a string containing HTML/JavaScript, it is rendered unescaped, enabling cross-site scripting in addition to the deserialization RCE.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (Cross-site Scripting)

extra.message: Authentication is performed by comparing request values to hardcoded credentials: if(password == "admin" and username == "admin"). The credentials are static, well-known, and compared in plaintext, allowing trivial login bypass.

The Flask SECRET_KEY is hardcoded as 'random'. Because Flask session cookies are signed with this key, anyone who knows it can forge session cookies (e.g. set session['loggedin']) and bypass the authentication check on /confidential.

The /webmaster route requires no authentication, yet it unconditionally sets session['loggedin'] = uuid.uuid1() for every visitor. The /confidential route trusts this session flag as proof of authentication, so any user can access the confidential page simply by visiting /webmaster first. The route also renders webmaster/index.html which exposes plaintext credentials.

Access control for /confidential is enforced only by 'if(session['loggedin'])'. This raises a KeyError (500, leaking a traceback in debug mode) for unauthenticated users rather than denying access cleanly, and the flag can be set by the unauthenticated /webmaster route or forged via the known SECRET_KEY. The page exposes confidential salary data, so the broken check is a real access-control bypass.

CORS is configured with resources={r"/*": {"origins": "*"}}, allowing any origin to make cross-origin requests to every route. Combined with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true set on /confidential (controllers/Confidential.py:10), this enables cross-origin reads of authenticated responses from any malicious site.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: Flask debug mode is enabled (app.debug = True). The Werkzeug debugger exposes interactive Python consoles and detailed stack traces (including sensitive data) on errors, which can lead to remote code execution if the debugger is reachable.

The webmaster template embeds and displays plaintext account credentials (e.g. Mark/Thisismysecretpass, Jacob/BirdLover1, Larry/Letmein123) in an HTML table. This page is served by the unauthenticated /webmaster route, exposing sensitive credentials to any visitor.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The database initialization script hardcodes user accounts with unsalted MD5 password hashes (e.g. Admin='0cef1fb10f60529028a71f58e54ed07b'). Hardcoded credential hashes committed to source are trivially crackable and constitute use of hard-coded credentials.
